lens: Boutique recruiter retrieval scanning and visual continuity; native Sessions and People, round 1

findings.criterion: Retrieval focus and interruption recovery at accessibility text size
findings.observation: At AX5 the shell truncates Sessions and People, expands the count/Synthetic preview band, and turns the generic composer into a large competing surface. The first record's topic or name is visible, but its full context and recency are not visible together in the initial capture. This finding concerns visible scanning cost; it does not establish that scrolling fails.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-09-06-ios-retrieval-craft/round-1/07-sessions-ax5.png and 08-people-ax5.png; compare the same full viewport shell with 01-sessions-light.png and 03-people-light.png. All are synthetic iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 native captures.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter returning between other tasks must parse incomplete navigation and spend more of the first viewport on utility controls before recovering the relationship context.
findings.recommendation: Use an accessibility-size shell layout with complete destination labels, compactly grouped supporting metadata, and a proportionate composer. Preserve search, filters, the selected text size, and access to every command.
findings.verification: Capture both pages at AX5 after adaptation, then perform page switching, search, filter, content scrolling, and return after interruption on the running app. Observe whether the correct record and its current context can be recovered without reconstructing the prior task.

findings.observation: At AX5 the People name is laid out as Leila / Hart- / mann beside a small initials circle, while the role/company then uses the full row width.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-09-06-ios-retrieval-craft/round-1/08-people-ax5.png, first record; compare 03-people-light.png and 06-people-dark-zh.png, where Leila Hartmann is intact and immediately legible.
findings.user_impact: The exact identity used to choose the person takes extra effort to read. Similar or long names could plausibly increase selection uncertainty, though the supplied fixture does not test that behavior.
findings.recommendation: Move to a full-width name grouping at accessibility sizes and position initials so they do not force surname hyphenation. Keep role, organization, and search context attached to that name.
findings.verification: Review AX5 captures with long, multiword, and similar names, then ask a recruiter to select a named person from a realistic list. Verify whole-word name readability and the correctness of the opened identity.

findings.observation: The read/unread light pair preserves the same Review needed label; the unread distinction appears only as a raised card. In the dark unread capture, the card and review-needed label again occur together without an independent unread label.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can plausibly read the card emphasis as work needing review and fail to distinguish it from content they have not read. The paired captures show separate visual state, but do not establish discoverability of its meaning.
findings.recommendation: Give unread a restrained independent cue, while leaving Review needed as an explicitly separate operational state.
findings.verification: Show the four read/unread and review-needed/not-needed combinations in both themes and ask an unfamiliar reviewer to identify both states. Then verify real read-state changes and persistence independently of review-needed state.

strengths: All eight full screenshots were inspected independently; no app source, other review, plan, or Simulator state was used.
At default size, session topics and People names are strong first reads; role, organization, search context, and recency remain quiet and legible in English light and Chinese dark UI.

Both pages show the same search/filter pattern. The active People filter in 04-people-filter.png visibly names Chief Product Officer search, offers an X affordance, and shows the narrowed single record; only the rendered state is established.
The sparse two-record fixture is honestly sparse, with restrained separators and no invented urgency, person rankings, decorative metrics, or row chevrons.

Scoped behavioral calibration: trigger relevance is 3 for the explicit retrieval job; visual interruption-recovery support is 2 because the large-text layout obscures immediate context; wedge discipline is 2 because generic input competes with retrieval at AX5. The reported 2 is the lowest material scoped dimension, not an average. Capture burden, source review, state integrity, action execution, and write safety are not scored from these still images.
missing_evidence: This pass_with_changes verdict is confined to the visual retrieval/scanning surface and is not approval of the complete capture-to-outcome workflow.

Executable search and filter behavior on both pages, empty-result reset, read/unread transitions and persistence, 44-point command targets, page navigation, and complete content access at AX5 remain pending.
Identity/provenance integrity and absence of unexpected external writes have not been verified from the supplied evidence.
No realistic-volume list, search collision, similarly named person, long localized identity, interruption return, or recruiter timing study is supplied.
Still images cannot establish VoiceOver semantics, tap behavior, scroll reachability, focus order, or accessibility conformance.
open_questions: Can an unfamiliar recruiter distinguish unread from review-needed in all four state combinations without an explanation?
After backgrounding or returning the next day, do query, filter, list position, and current identity remain understandable and correct?
